llm.summary: This is a disclosed anti-detection browser automation skill, but it strongly steers agents toward bypassing bot defenses and using authenticated cookies/proxies, so users should review it carefully before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill depends on a patched Firefox browser, Xvfb/system libraries, local service access, optional residential proxies and GeoIP masking, and authenticated browsing support, which is high-impact and not tightly scoped to first-party or consented targets.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifacts disclose Node, a local localhost:9377 service, system browser dependencies, and a startup script that launches a background node server with nohup; this is coherent for browser automation but should be administratively reviewed.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Agent instructions prefer camofox tools for external public sites, recommend scraping bot-hardened sites, suggest retrying with different timing when CAPTCHA or block pages appear, and include arbitrary page JavaScript evaluation; this is broader than neutral authorized browsing.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Cookie import treats session cookies as live credentials and session persistence is documented under ~/.camofox/profiles; cookie import is disabled by default and warnings exist, but README/AGENTS still promote authenticated scraping and lack strong user-confirmation controls.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is advanced browser automation, but the README and agent instructions make anti-detection and bypass of CAPTCHAs, WAFs, Cloudflare, and commercial bot detection a core value proposition, including scraping and login-wall use cases.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only in a controlled environment and only for sites, accounts, sessions, and proxies you are explicitly authorized to use. Treat imported cookies as full account credentials, protect or avoid CAMOFOX_API_KEY, require access control for the local service, and do not use this skill to bypass CAPTCHAs, WAFs, bot defenses, or scrape behind login walls without clear permission.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The node dependency, local server, and browser process are expected for this kind of automation and are partly disclosed in SKILL metadata, but the broader authority is not expressed through a clear permission model.
[SQP-2] expected: Cookie import is a disclosed feature and SKILL.md warns that cookies are bearer tokens, but README.md and AGENTS.md promote behind-login browsing/scraping without equally strong consent and handling guardrails.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The CAPTCHA/block retry guidance and scraping-oriented examples are not acceptable as ordinary browser automation scoping because they encourage working around third-party anti-abuse controls.
[SQP-2] expected: Proxy and GeoIP routing fit the anti-detection purpose, but the artifacts do not provide enough limits around lawful proxy provenance, attribution, or target authorization.
[SSD-2] unexpected: The evasion-oriented marketing is artifact-backed: README.md repeatedly claims undetectability and bypass of named defenses, which materially raises abuse risk despite authorized-use warnings in SKILL.md.
